# Job Search Assistant — Implementation Plan

## Context

The user is job hunting and wants a personal tool that aggregates candidate job postings, ranks them by predicted interest-fit and candidate-fit, helps tailor resumes/cover letters from their document history, tracks applications, and learns their preferences from interested/not-interested feedback over time. There is no existing code for this — it's a clean-slate build.

This will **not** live inside the public `projects` portfolio repo. That repo publishes a README + screenshots per project, and one project (Shelf Life) even has a public dev changelog — unsuitable for data this sensitive (resume contents, target companies, application statuses). Instead it's a **new, standalone private repo**: `job-search-assistant`.

The closest architectural relative is `projects/01 - Shelf Life (Goodreads Recommender v2)`, which the user wants reused as a pattern: FastAPI + uv backend, React/Vite/TS frontend (Context state, no UI library), multi-stage Dockerfile, `make deploy` → Cloud Build → Cloud Run, Secret-Manager-gated Anthropic key. The key structural difference: Shelf Life is stateless and public (browser holds all state, precomputed artifacts, `--allow-unauthenticated`). This app is single-user, needs durable server-side writes (jobs, tracker, feedback), runs a scheduled background job daily, and must be locked down to just the user.

**Key constraints established during planning** (not to be re-litigated):
- LinkedIn/Indeed/Glassdoor have no real public job-search API — these are handled via manual paste-in (URL or raw text), parsed into structured fields by Claude. Automated aggregation instead comes from legitimate aggregator APIs (Adzuna, RemoteOK), direct polling of public ATS job-board APIs (Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby — these are intentionally public/embeddable endpoints, not scraping) for companies the user lists, and a generic **custom board** adapter the user can point at any URL — this covers both a single company's `/careers` page *and* niche multi-employer boards the user specifically wants tracked (e.g. techjobsforgov.com), since both are "fetch a listing page, let Claude extract postings from it."
- Claude (Anthropic API) does the real reasoning: parsing paste-ins, interest/candidate-fit scoring (High/Med/Low), resume/cover-letter tailoring, and resume-history synthesis into a candidate profile. To control cost, a cheap rule-based pre-filter runs before any LLM call, and a configurable daily cap (default 50) limits full LLM scoring passes, with unprocessed jobs carried over at higher priority the next day. Every Claude call is logged (type, job, tokens, estimated cost) so the user can see exactly which jobs got the LLM treatment and what it's costing.
- Preference learning from interested/not-interested marks plus application outcomes is a maintained **preference profile** (a text summary Claude updates periodically from new signal) injected into future scoring prompts — not a trained numeric model. Application progression (applied → interview → offer) is weighted as the strongest signal, stronger than a bare "interested" mark.
- Resume/cover-letter generation is a manual, per-job action the user triggers only when they decide to apply — not run automatically for every high-ranking job — to avoid paying for generation on jobs that never go anywhere.
- Deployed to Cloud Run + Cloud Scheduler (same GCP account/pattern as Shelf Life) for the daily job to run even when the laptop is off.
- Because this holds sensitive personal data, the deployed service must be locked to the user's own Google account — via Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) on the Cloud Run service, not Shelf Life's `--allow-unauthenticated` pattern.

## Repo layout

New repo: `job-search-assistant`, Python package `src/jobhunt/`, mirroring Shelf Life's top-level shape (`src/`, `frontend/`, `config/`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, `tests/`). No portfolio README entry, no public changelog/prompts-log machinery — those were specific to Shelf Life's public-facing changelog feature, not a general requirement.

## Data model (SQLite, raw `sqlite3` + `schema.sql`, no ORM)

- `sources` — monitored companies/boards: `kind` (`aggregator_adzuna|aggregator_remoteok|ats_greenhouse|ats_lever|ats_ashby|custom_board`), config, poll frequency, last-poll bookkeeping. `custom_board` is the generic "any URL" adapter: a single company's careers page or a niche multi-employer board (e.g. techjobsforgov.com) — the user adds it via `SourcesPage` by pasting a URL, and Claude extracts one or many postings from whatever listing page comes back.
- `jobs` — normalized postings: title/company/location/remote_type/salary range/description/url/posted_at/first_seen_at/last_seen_at, `dedupe_key` (hash of normalized company+title+location or canonical URL, unique), `status` (active/expired/removed), `needs_review` for unconfirmed manual paste-ins.
- `scoring_queue` — the pre-filter → LLM cap/backlog mechanism: `prefilter_score`, `priority`, `status` (pending/in_progress/scored/skipped).
- `job_scores` — one row per scoring pass: `interest_fit`/`candidate_fit` (High/Med/Low) + numeric scores, `summary_text`, `rationale_text`, model/prompt version.
- `digest_entries` — materializes each day's ranked list (`digest_date, job_id, rank`) so past digests stay stable/browsable.
- `feedback` — `interested|not_interested|maybe` + optional note, per job.
- `applications` + `application_status_history` — tracker state and its timeline.
- `resumes` — uploaded resume/cover-letter files + extracted raw text.
- `candidate_profile` (+ history) — Claude-synthesized career-progression/competency narrative from all resumes.
- `preference_profile` (+ history) — Claude-maintained summary of what the user responds to, rebuilt from accumulated feedback and application outcomes (the latter weighted as the strongest signal — see below).
- `generated_documents` — tailored resumes/cover letters per job.
- `settings` — runtime-editable preferences (daily cap, prefilter keywords/titles/locations, salary floor, remote policy) so Settings-page edits don't need a redeploy.
- `runs` — observability for each daily pipeline run (counts, cap usage, carry-over, errors).
- `llm_calls` — one row per Claude API call of any kind (`call_type`: scoring/parsing/generation/profile_rebuild/career_profile; `job_id` when applicable; input/output tokens; estimated cost; timestamp; model). Backs the usage log (below) so the user can see exactly which jobs got the LLM treatment and what it cost.

## Backend architecture (`src/jobhunt/`)

**Routes** (`api/`): `jobs.py` (list/detail/patch, `POST /api/jobs/manual` for paste-in → Claude-parsed draft awaiting confirmation, feedback endpoint), `digest.py` (today/by-date/date-list), `applications.py` (CRUD + status transitions writing history), `sources.py` (CRUD + dry-run test-fetch), `resumes.py` (upload/list/delete, profile rebuild), `generate.py` (tailored resume/cover-letter generation), `settings.py`, `internal.py` (`POST /internal/run-daily`, the Cloud Scheduler target, gated by a dedicated secret header independent of IAP).

**Ingest adapters** (`ingest/`): `adapters/greenhouse.py`, `lever.py`, `ashby.py` (public per-company job-board JSON endpoints), `adapters/adzuna.py`, `remoteok.py` (keyed/open aggregator feeds), `adapters/custom_board.py` (httpx fetch with content-hash caching + Claude-assisted extraction, since arbitrary listing pages — one company's careers page or a niche multi-employer board — have no fixed schema; may extract multiple postings per fetch), `manual_import.py` (paste-in → Claude structured extraction → editable draft, never silently trusted).

**Daily pipeline** (`pipeline/daily_run.py`, orchestrating `core/prefilter.py`, `core/queue.py`, `core/scoring.py`):
1. Poll enabled sources → upsert `jobs` (dedupe on `dedupe_key`; unseen-in-N-days → `expired`).
2. Rule-based pre-filter (keyword/title/location/salary against `settings`) scores and queues new/changed jobs.
3. Select the top `settings.daily_llm_cap` pending jobs by `priority` (pre-filter score + age bonus, so nothing is starved) and mark in-progress.
4. For each, call Claude with the job text + `candidate_profile` + `preference_profile` + recent raw feedback → write `job_scores`; log the call in `llm_calls`.
5. Anything beyond the cap stays `pending`, reconsidered next run at higher priority — this is the backlog carry-over.
6. Build today's `digest_entries` from fresh scores.
7. Conditionally regenerate `preference_profile` (only once enough new signal has accumulated or enough time has passed, to bound Claude calls) — see weighting below.
8. Write a `runs` row.

**Preference-profile signal weighting**: the rebuild prompt is fed both `feedback` rows and `applications`/`application_status_history`, with application outcomes weighted as the strongest signal — a job that reached `interview` or `offer` says far more about genuine fit than a bare "interested" mark, and a `rejected`/`withdrawn` application is informative too (though Claude is told to distinguish "wasn't a candidate fit" from "wasn't actually interested," since a rejection conflates both). Bare `feedback` marks are the weakest, fastest-arriving signal and mainly useful for quick signal between application-level events.

**Resume/cover-letter generation trigger**: `generate.py` is invoked only from a user action on a specific job — either `JobDetailPage`'s "Generate for this application" button or directly from `ApplicationTrackerPage` when adding a job — not automatically for every high-ranking digest entry. This keeps generation cost tied 1:1 to jobs the user actually decides to pursue.

**Resume ingestion / candidate profile** (`core/resume_parse.py` via pypdf/python-docx/plain text; `core/profile.py` synthesizes `candidate_profile` from all resume/cover-letter text via one Claude call).

**Generation** (`core/generate.py`): tailored resume/cover-letter text per job, stored in `generated_documents`.

## Frontend architecture (`frontend/`, React 19 + Vite + TS, no UI library)

Pages: `DigestPage` (default route — ranked jobs with location/salary/summary/posted-age/ratings, past-digest browsing, interested/not-interested actions), `JobDetailPage` (full description, scoring rationale, generate resume/cover letter when pursuing it, add to tracker), `ApplicationTrackerPage` (status pipeline + per-application timeline), `SourcesPage` (manage monitored companies/ATS boards/custom boards incl. niche multi-employer boards + manual paste-in, test-fetch), `ResumesPage` (upload, extracted text, candidate-profile view/rebuild), `SettingsPage` (pre-filter rules, daily cap, preference-profile viewer/rebuild, **Usage log**: recent `llm_calls` with per-call cost and a running daily/monthly total).

Unlike Shelf Life (all state in localStorage, stateless API), the source of truth here is server-persisted SQLite — `store.tsx` keeps the same Context + mutation-function shape but each mutation calls the backend and updates a local cache, rather than writing straight to localStorage. Only pure UI prefs (last-viewed digest date, tracker view mode) stay in localStorage.

**Default application status pipeline**: `saved → applied → phone_screen → interview → offer | rejected | withdrawn` (rejected/withdrawn reachable from any non-terminal state).

## Deploy

Dockerfile mirrors Shelf Life's two-stage shape (`node:22-slim` builds `frontend/dist`, `python:3.12-slim` + `uv sync --frozen --no-default-groups` runs uvicorn) — no precomputed-artifacts copy step needed.

**Persistence**: Cloud Run instances are ephemeral by default; this app needs a durable SQLite file + uploaded resume blobs across restarts/deploys. Use Cloud Run's GCS-bucket volume mount for the SQLite file and resume storage, with `--max-instances 1` (single personal user, avoids SQLite multi-writer issues entirely).

**Access control**: enable Identity-Aware Proxy on the Cloud Run service (Cloud Run keeps `--no-allow-unauthenticated`; IAP sits in front and handles Google sign-in), granting the "IAP-secured Web App User" role to the user's own Google account only. This replaces Shelf Life's `--allow-unauthenticated` pattern entirely — the whole point here is that nobody else can ever reach it. The `/internal/run-daily` endpoint for Cloud Scheduler is a separate concern, gated by its own secret header (Scheduler can't do interactive Google sign-in).

**Secrets** (Secret Manager, same `make <name>-secret` pattern as Shelf Life's `chat-secret`): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ADZUNA_APP_ID`/`ADZUNA_APP_KEY`, `SCHEDULER_SECRET`. Makefile adds a `scheduler-setup` target creating/updating the Cloud Scheduler job (daily cron → `POST /internal/run-daily` with the secret header).

**Resume ingestion path**: production path is browser upload via `ResumesPage`. Since "local files I'll point it to" can't apply once deployed (Cloud Run can't read the user's laptop filesystem), add a small local CLI (`uv run python -m jobhunt.cli.ingest_resumes <folder>`) for one-time bulk import into the local dev DB before the first deploy, if there are many historical files to seed.

## Milestones (each independently demoable)

1. **Scaffold + data model + resume ingestion** — uv/FastAPI/React scaffold, full `schema.sql`, resume upload + parsing, candidate-profile generation. *Demo: upload a resume, see extracted text + generated profile.*
2. **Manual paste-in + LLM scoring + Digest UI** — `/api/jobs/manual`, `job_scores`, `DigestPage`. *Demo: paste a job URL/text, see it scored and appear in the digest.*
3. **Feedback loop + Application tracker** — feedback capture, preference-profile generation + injection into scoring, applications + tracker UI. *Demo: mark jobs interested/not-interested, rebuild the preference profile, see it affect a new job's scoring rationale; move a job through tracker statuses.*
4. **Automated source adapters + pre-filter + daily cap/queue + usage log** — `SourcesPage`, Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby + Adzuna/RemoteOK adapters, `custom_board` adapter, pre-filter, scoring queue, `llm_calls` logging + Usage log view, `/internal/run-daily` (manually triggered for now). *Demo: add a company board + a custom board like techjobsforgov.com, run the endpoint, watch ingestion → pre-filter → capped scoring → digest, and see each scoring call show up in the usage log with its cost; exceed the cap and confirm carry-over on the next run.*
5. **Resume/cover-letter tailoring** — generation endpoints + `JobDetailPage`/tracker "generate for this application" action. *Demo: mark a job as one you're applying to, generate a tailored resume + cover letter for it; confirm it's not offered for jobs you haven't decided to pursue.*
6. **Cloud Run + Cloud Scheduler deploy** — Dockerfile, Makefile deploy targets, Secret Manager secrets, GCS volume for SQLite, IAP lock-down, Cloud Scheduler job. *Demo: sign in with the user's Google account at the deployed URL, see the digest; confirm the daily job fires on its own overnight.*

## Open defaults (flagged, not blocking)

- **Aggregator APIs for M4**: Adzuna + RemoteOK to start (broad, free-tier, simple REST); USAJobs or others only if the user wants that coverage later.
- **Posted-date gaps**: some ATS responses/custom pages lack a reliable posted date — fall back to "first seen N days ago" (`jobs.first_seen_at`).
- **Initial source list** (which companies/boards to monitor, target titles/keywords/locations) is left as user-entered config via `SourcesPage`/`SettingsPage` after M1 ships, not hardcoded.

## Verification

- Each milestone ships with its own demo path (above) runnable via `make serve` + `make dev` locally, following Shelf Life's dev loop.
- `tests/` (pytest) covers: dedupe logic, pre-filter scoring, queue priority/carry-over math, status-transition validity, and adapter normalization (with recorded fixture responses for each ATS/aggregator, no live network calls in CI).
- Before M6, run the full pipeline locally end-to-end (`/internal/run-daily` curl'd) against real configured sources to sanity-check volume and cap behavior before paying for Cloud Run + Scheduler.
- After M6, confirm IAP actually blocks unauthenticated access (test from a logged-out browser/incognito) before relying on it for sensitive data.

<details><summary>Claude's plan (approved)</summary>

# Resume generation rewrite: context-anchored edits instead of rebuild-from-scratch

## Context

The user reports that generated resumes are "consistently poorly formatted" — bad enough that fixing them by hand would take longer than writing the resume from scratch. They floated converting the resume to a Google Doc and submitting suggested edits via the Docs API as a possible fix, and asked if other solutions made more sense.

Investigation found the exact root cause: `write_resume_docx()` in `docx_writer.py` **deletes the entire document body and rebuilds it from six cloned "exemplar" paragraphs** (one Title, one Heading, one bullet, one bold-header line, one contact line, one blank spacer), captured once from the template. Every bullet in the whole rebuilt document reuses that *one* exemplar's paragraph XML, so if the real resume has multiple jobs with distinct bullet-list numbering definitions (`numPr`/`numId`), tables (a two-column layout), or any paragraph-specific formatting beyond the single captured exemplar of each role, all of that is discarded. By contrast, `write_cover_letter_docx()` in the same file already does **positional in-place text replacement** on the existing paragraphs — it never deletes/rebuilds — and isn't reported as broken. That contrast is the direct evidence pointing at the fix: stop reconstructing the resume from scratch; edit the real template in place, like the cover letter path already does, just more surgically.

Separately, I found that Google recently (GA rollout starting 2026-09-30) added a native "suggested edit" mode to the Docs API (`batchUpdate` with `writeControl.writeMode: "SUGGEST"`), which would have made the user's original Google Docs idea far less costly to build than it would have been a few months ago. I presented both options — real Google Docs suggestions (requires new OAuth/Drive integration, a stored credential, and index-based editing against the Docs API) vs. the same "anchored edit" idea applied locally to the `.docx` as native Word tracked changes (`<w:ins>`/`<w:del>`), with zero new infrastructure — and the user chose **the local `.docx` approach**. A `.docx` with tracked changes still opens fine in Google Docs, which renders Word's tracked changes as its own Suggesting-mode review UI natively (a long-standing, unrelated Google Docs capability) — so the review experience the user wanted is preserved without adding OAuth, a service account, or any new dependency.

Cover letters are **out of scope**: `write_cover_letter_docx` isn't broken in the way resumes are (no delete-and-rebuild), and the user's complaint was specifically about resumes. Don't touch it.

## Approach

Replace the "generate a whole new resume from scratch" model with a **context-anchored edit** model: Claude is shown the original resume's own paragraphs (text + a role tag: title/contact/heading/job_header/bullet/description/normal), and instead of generating a full new document, proposes a short list of edit operations, each anchored to one paragraph's **exact existing text**:

- `replace` — reword a specific line in place (e.g. tailor a bullet's wording).
- `insert_after` — add a brand-new line immediately after an existing one, inheriting that exact neighbor's formatting (fixes the multi-list/numbering bug directly: a new bullet under Job A clones Job A's own `numPr`, not some global exemplar's).
- `delete` — remove a line that isn't relevant to this posting.

These ops are applied to a fresh copy of the user's real template as native Word tracked-changes markup (`<w:ins>`/`<w:del>`, including marking the paragraph *mark* itself as inserted/deleted so Accept/Reject in Word cleanly adds/removes whole lines, not just text). Every paragraph not targeted by an op is left **byte-for-byte untouched** — this is what actually fixes the formatting problem, since nothing is ever reconstructed from a lossy exemplar.

This also reverses last session's `GENERATED_FONT = "Calibri"` hardcoding for the resume path: that was a reasonable patch for the old "rebuild everything from one exemplar" model, but is wrong for this new model. New/replaced text should instead inherit font name **and** size from the *specific* anchor paragraph's own run (`<w:rPr>` deep-copy), which generalizes correctly to any user's resume and any inconsistency within it, without hardcoding a font name. `write_cover_letter_docx`'s existing `GENERATED_FONT`/`_set_plain`/`_set_bold_split` helpers are untouched (cover letters keep today's behavior).

### New Pydantic models (`src/jobhunt/core/docx_writer.py`)

Replace `ResumeContent`/`ResumeSection`/`ResumeLine` entirely with:

```python
class TemplateLine(BaseModel):
    role: Literal["title", "contact", "heading", "job_header", "bullet", "description", "normal"]
    text: str            # exact paragraph text, verbatim
    section: str | None  # nearest preceding heading's text, e.g. "WORK EXPERIENCE"
    under: str | None    # nearest preceding job_header's text, e.g. "ACME CORP | Senior Engineer"

class ResumeEditOp(BaseModel):
    op: Literal["replace", "insert_after", "delete"]
    anchor_text: str
    new_text: str | None = None
    bold_part: str | None = None   # only for anchors with a bold+nonbold split (job_header lines)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_fields_for_op(self) -> "ResumeEditOp": ...  # replace/insert_after require new_text;
                                                            # delete must not set new_text/bold_part

class ResumeEditPlan(BaseModel):
    ops: list[ResumeEditOp]
```

A flat model (one `op` enum + optional fields, validated post-hoc) is used instead of a discriminated union of per-op-type models, because it's unconfirmed whether `client.messages.parse(output_format=...)` robustly supports a discriminated union nested inside a list — this codebase has only ever used single flat models with `output_format`. **First implementation step: a short throwaway script calling `client.messages.parse(output_format=ResumeEditPlan)` against the real API to confirm the shape works before building the writer around it.**

### Extracting addressable lines (`docx_writer.py`, new function)

```python
def extract_addressable_lines(template_path: Path) -> list[TemplateLine]:
```

Walks `Document(template_path).paragraphs` (same top-level, table-skipping enumeration `write_cover_letter_docx` already uses — **not** `resume_parse.py`'s `_iter_block_items`, which exists for a different concern: flattening table content into `candidate_profile` text. Reusing it here would let Claude anchor on text inside a table cell that the writer can't locate/mutate. Table-based resumes stay an explicit, documented unsupported case — same scope as today, not a regression). Skips blank paragraphs entirely (never addressable — anchoring on `""` would be hopelessly ambiguous). Classifies every non-blank paragraph's `role` using the same style-name heuristics `_capture_exemplars` already uses, but applied to *every* paragraph instead of just the first of each kind — this per-paragraph tagging (vs. one global exemplar per role) is the structural fix. Tracks `section`/`under` as running state while iterating in document order.

### New writer function (`docx_writer.py`, replaces `write_resume_docx`)

```python
def write_resume_edits(template_path: Path, ops: list[ResumeEditOp], output_path: Path) -> None:
```

**Two-phase: resolve every op's anchor first, mutate nothing until all resolve cleanly.**

Phase 1 — for each op, exact-match `op.anchor_text` against every top-level paragraph's `.text`:
- Zero matches → `AnchorNotFoundError`.
- 2+ matches → `AmbiguousAnchorError` (no silent pick, ever — duplicate bullet wording across two jobs is a realistic failure mode, not just a hypothetical).
- Resolves to a `title`/`contact` line → `DisallowedAnchorError` (hard code-level denylist — a name/contact line should never vary by job, so block it unconditionally rather than relying on prompt compliance alone).

Phase 2 — only after every op validates, apply mutations and `doc.save()` once at the end, so one bad op in an otherwise-valid plan writes nothing to disk.

Per-op OOXML approach:
- **`replace`**: relabel the matched run(s) as deleted — `<w:del>` wrapping a `<w:r>` that deep-copies the *original run's own* `<w:rPr>` with `<w:t>` → `<w:delText>` (preserves bold/italic/font/size automatically, since it's the same `rPr` the run always had). Insert a new `<w:ins>`-wrapped run (or two, for a `bold_part` split) immediately after, cloning the matched run's `rPr` for the new text's formatting.
- **`insert_after`**: deep-copy the *entire anchor paragraph element* (so the clone gets that paragraph's own `pPr`/`numPr`/indentation — not a global exemplar's), mark its paragraph mark as inserted (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:ins .../></w:rPr></w:pPr>`), replace its run text, wrap the run(s) in `<w:ins>`, insert the finished paragraph immediately after the anchor in the body.
- **`delete`**: wrap the matched paragraph's existing run(s) in `<w:del>`/`<w:delText>` and mark its paragraph mark deleted the same way `insert_after` marks one inserted — but leave the paragraph element in the tree (removing it ourselves would make the deletion permanent with no tracked-changes record, defeating the point).

All `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` elements in one call share one `w:author = "Job Search Assistant"` and one `w:date` timestamp, with a `w:id` counter seeded past any id already present in the template.

`AnchorNotFoundError`/`AmbiguousAnchorError`/`DisallowedAnchorError` are plain `Exception` subclasses, deliberately **not** `TemplateError` — `TemplateError` means "template unusable, fall back to plain text silently" (existing, intentional); these three mean "Claude's proposed edit doesn't line up with this template," a failed generation attempt that must surface as an error, not degrade silently.

### Changes in `core/generate.py`

- `RESUME_STRUCTURED_SYSTEM_PROMPT` rewritten to describe the edit model: anchor text must be copied character-for-character from the supplied line list; `replace` should keep roughly the same length (protects one-page fit, now a much more robust guarantee than last session's prompt-wording tweak since ops are small/local rather than whole-document regeneration); never anchor on `title`/`contact`; never change an employer/title-held/date inside a `job_header` line even via `replace`; keep net new-line count small; never fabricate.
- `generate_resume()`: calls `extract_addressable_lines(template_path)`, serializes it into the prompt, calls `client.messages.parse(..., output_format=ResumeEditPlan)`, calls `write_resume_edits(...)` inside the existing `try/except TemplateError` / generic `Exception` fallback block (unchanged structurally — a bad template still degrades to plain text). The three new anchor-resolution errors are **not** added to that except block — they propagate out of `generate_resume()` uncaught, so they reach the API layer as real errors instead of a silently-wrong plain-text fallback.
- `content_text` (used in the API response regardless of docx success) is computed by applying `plan.ops` to the already-validated `(lines, ops)` pair in pure Python and rendering the result with the same markdown shape `_render_resume_markdown` used — **not** by re-reading the output `.docx`'s tracked-changes XML back into text, since python-docx's `.text` only sees direct `<w:r>` children and would conflate `<w:delText>` with surviving text (the same blind spot the existing hyperlink-stripping regression test documents for `<w:hyperlink>`).
- `_generate_resume_plain` and the "no usable template" branch are unchanged — confirmed orthogonal, that fallback triggers before any of this runs.
- `write_cover_letter_docx`, `CoverLetterContent`, `COVER_LETTER_STRUCTURED_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `generate_cover_letter` — **untouched**.

### Changes in `api/generate.py`

One new `except` clause in the resume route, alongside the existing `ValidationError`/`ValueError`/`LLMError` handling:

```python
except (AnchorNotFoundError, AmbiguousAnchorError, DisallowedAnchorError) as exc:
    raise HTTPException(502, f"the tailored edits didn't line up with your resume template ({exc}) — try again") from exc
```

## Reused existing code

- `write_cover_letter_docx`'s positional in-place editing *pattern* (the template this whole rewrite generalizes) — not literally called, but the model to follow.
- `_clear_runs`, `_get_sect_pr`, `_first_nonempty_run` — kept as-is for the cover-letter path; the new resume code writes its own run-construction logic rather than reusing `_set_plain`/`_set_bold_split`, since those unconditionally force `GENERATED_FONT` (exactly the behavior being reversed for resumes).
- `_capture_exemplars`'s style-name → role classification heuristics — reused (generalized to tag every paragraph, not just one exemplar per role) inside the new `extract_addressable_lines`.
- The existing `llm_error_boundary`/`log_call` pattern in `core/llm.py` for the new `messages.parse` call.
- The existing `ValidationError`-before-`ValueError` catch ordering in `api/generate.py` (Pydantic v2 quirk) — the new `model_validator` on `ResumeEditOp` raises into that same `ValidationError` path for free when Claude's op shape is malformed.

## Critical files

- `src/jobhunt/core/docx_writer.py` — new models, `extract_addressable_lines`, `write_resume_edits`, three new exception types; delete `ResumeContent`/`ResumeSection`/`ResumeLine`/`write_resume_docx`.
- `src/jobhunt/core/generate.py` — new prompt, rewired `generate_resume()`, new `content_text` rendering from `(lines, ops)`.
- `src/jobhunt/api/generate.py` — one new except clause.
- `tests/test_docx_writer.py` — delete the Calibri-forcing resume test (behavior being reversed); rewrite the margins/styles and unrecognizable-template resume tests for the new functions; add ~13 new tests per the test plan below; cover-letter tests untouched.
- `tests/test_generate.py` — swap `ResumeContent(...)` fixture construction for `ResumeEditPlan(...)` with real anchor text matching `_make_resume_docx`'s actual paragraphs (e.g. anchor `"Did an old thing."`) in every test that builds one directly; add one new 502 test for a bogus anchor; rewrite `test_generate_resume_uses_docx_template_when_available`'s assertion (name is now *never* rewritten by design — assert `"OLD NAME"` is **still present**, and that a bullet changed instead); cover-letter and plain-text-path tests untouched.

## New tests to add

In `tests/test_docx_writer.py`: `extract_addressable_lines` role-tagging + blank-skipping; `extract_addressable_lines` section/under tracking across a heading→job_header→bullets sequence; `replace` touches only the targeted paragraph (every other paragraph's XML byte-identical before/after); `replace` produces real `<w:del>`/`<w:ins>` XML with id/author/date, not just updated flattened text; `replace` on a bold+nonbold line preserves bold/non-bold split; `insert_after` clones the *correct* anchor's `numPr` (two jobs with different list configs — direct regression test for the original bug); `insert_after` marks both run content and paragraph mark as inserted; `delete` marks both run content and paragraph mark as deleted while leaving the element in the tree; `AnchorNotFoundError`/`AmbiguousAnchorError`/`DisallowedAnchorError` each raise correctly; font+size on new content come from the specific anchor's own run (two paragraphs in visibly different fonts, each edit matches its own anchor); a plan with one invalid op writes nothing to `output_path`.

In `tests/test_generate.py`: a bogus `anchor_text` in the fake LLM response surfaces as a 502 with an actionable message through the real route.

## Verification

- `uv run --with ruff ruff check .` and `PYTHONPATH=src uv run pytest -q` after implementation.
- Before trusting the generated output's formatting, **open real generated output in actual Word (and ideally Google Docs via upload) and manually Accept/Reject a `replace`, an `insert_after`, and a `delete`** — passing pytest only proves the XML is well-formed and python-docx can re-read it, not that Word/Google Docs render the Accept/Reject behavior cleanly for a paragraph-mark-level tracked change (a known sharp edge in OOXML). This is the real test of whether the formatting problem is actually fixed.
- Smoke-test `POST /api/generate/resume` against the live dev server with a real job + the user's real uploaded resume, and have the user open the resulting `.docx` themselves to judge whether review/accept now feels like the "edit, not regenerate" experience they wanted.
- Confirm the discriminated-structured-output risk early: run the `client.messages.parse(output_format=ResumeEditPlan)` spike against the real API before writing the rest of the writer around its assumed shape.
